items.question: What claim of difference arises from commander and commanded roles?
premises: One is taken as commander
Another is taken as commanded
Such roles imply difference between two
items.inference: The sense of commander and commanded establishes a division between self and other.
items.plain_english: You are the commander and I am the one to be commanded; thus there is a difference between us.

items.question: Who truly mounts and rides as the horse-rider, O god?
premises: A horse-rider is imagined as mounting
Mounting implies a distinct agent
The question challenges that agency
items.inference: The identity of the true rider is called into question.
items.plain_english: O god, who is it that mounts and rides as the horse-rider?

items.question: Who is the fit rider able to use the foot-instrument there?
premises: A foot-instrument is present for riding
Riding requires a fit rider
The fit rider is not identified
items.inference: The verse presses for identification of the one truly capable of riding.
items.plain_english: Tell me, who is the fit rider there for the foot-instrument?

items.question: Does that same horse-rider truly mount and ride upon the horse?
premises: A specific rider is indicated
Mounting is attributed to that rider
The attribution remains under inquiry
items.inference: The verse continues questioning the reality of the rider's agency.
items.plain_english: Does that horse-rider mount and ride upon it?

rows.grounds: having nature of sound and point

items.question: What is the nature of that unborn reality beyond name, form, and color?
premises: That reality lacks name form and color
That reality is unborn
That reality is of sound and point nature
items.inference: The ultimate reality is described as unborn and beyond ordinary attributes yet characterized as sound and point.
items.plain_english: He is without name, form, and color, unborn, and of the nature of sound and point.

items.question: How should one perceive the moving and non-moving world in relation to Śiva?
premises: The world includes moving and non-moving
The world is made of Śiva
One is urged to see this
items.inference: The entire world should be recognized as pervaded by and consisting of Śiva.
items.plain_english: See the moving and non-moving world as made of Śiva.

items.question: What primordial reality called Śiva is described as freed from inertia?
premises: A primordial reality is named Śiva
It is freed from inertia
It is likened to clear water
items.inference: The primordial Śiva is pure and free from insentience like clear water.
items.plain_english: The primordial reality called Śiva is like water, freed from inertia.

items.question: Why must one bring about the union of mind and breath?
premises: Mind and breath are distinct
Their union can be effected
The verse commands making that union
items.inference: Practice requires intentionally uniting mind and breath.
items.plain_english: Bring about the union of mind and breath.

rows.grounds: for the sake of pervading that

items.question: What practice enables pervasion of that reality according to this teaching?
premises: Pervasion of that reality is sought
Breath and mind can become one
Oneness is presented as the means
items.inference: The oneness of breath and mind is the means for pervading that reality.
items.plain_english: For the sake of pervading that, there must indeed be oneness of breath and mind.

items.question: What impurity falls upon the mirror through the effect of breath?
premises: A mirror can receive impurity
Breath can affect the mirror
The nature of that impurity is questioned
items.inference: The verse uses the mirror image to question how impurity appears.
items.plain_english: What impurity falls upon the mirror from breath?

items.question: How does an indifferent mirror acquire impurity from external dust particles?
premises: A mirror can be indifferent
Dust particles can settle on it
Settled dust appears as impurity
items.inference: Impurity arises from external contact, not from the mirror's own nature.
items.plain_english: Just as an indifferent mirror becomes stained by dust particles.

items.question: What remains when repeated affirmations and negations of someone are exhausted?
premises: Someone is alternately posited and negated
The pattern repeats multiple times
The questioning seeks what remains
items.inference: Repeated positing and negating undermines fixed identification.
items.plain_english: Someone, not; someone, not; someone, not—what then?

items.question: What destination remains to be reached in this state of realization?
premises: A goal might be assumed
The verse negates any such goal
The negation is stated firmly
items.inference: In this realization there is nothing further to be reached.
items.plain_english: Here, there is firmly nothing at all to be reached.

items.question: What constitutes the true practice of one who knows reality?
premises: A knower of reality engages in practice
That practice is specifically identified
The verse points to that practice
items.inference: The verse defines the practice proper to the knower of reality.
items.plain_english: That is the practice of the knower of reality.

items.question: Why is this practice proclaimed as the practice of reality by the wise?
premises: This is called practice of reality
Foremost wise ones proclaim it
Their proclamation gives it authority
items.inference: The wise authorities identify this as the true practice of reality.
items.plain_english: This has been proclaimed as the practice of reality by the foremost wise ones.

items.question: For whom does drinking the pure nectar of knowledge become liberation?
premises: Pure nectar of knowledge is available
Liberation is linked to it
The recipient of liberation is questioned
items.inference: The verse asks who attains liberation through the pure nectar of knowledge.
items.plain_english: For whom is there liberation through the pure nectar of knowledge?

rows.grounds: abiding in drinking the nectar of pure knowledge

items.question: What state is characterized by abiding in the drinking of pure knowledge nectar?
premises: Pure knowledge is likened to nectar
One may drink that nectar
Abiding in that drinking defines a state
items.inference: The described state is one of stable absorption in pure knowledge.
items.plain_english: Abiding in the drinking of the nectar of pure knowledge.

items.question: How is the worship of Śiva realized as light within the mind and self?
premises: Worship of Śiva is invoked
Light is associated with mind and self
The verse locates worship inwardly
items.inference: True worship of Śiva is an inner illumination in mind and self.
items.plain_english: The worship of Śiva is the light of the mind in the self.

rows.grounds: the rāhu of one's own I-ness

items.question: What immediately swallows the eclipsing force of one's own I-ness?
premises: Own I-ness acts like an eclipsing rāhu
That eclipsing force can be swallowed
The swallowing happens immediately
items.inference: The grasping of egoic I-ness is immediately overcome by a higher recognition.
items.plain_english: And it immediately swallows the Rāhu of one's own I-ness.

items.question: What remains to be lifted when repeated efforts reveal nothing to lift?
premises: Lifting is repeatedly attempted
The attempt finds nothing lifted
The absence of an object is emphasized
items.inference: The verse negates any separate object that could be lifted.
items.plain_english: Lift, lift—then nothing at all is lifted.

rows.grounds: of one nature as pure knowledge

items.question: What sole nature remains when reality is recognized as pure knowledge alone?
premises: Reality is described as pure knowledge
That knowledge is one nature
The description is emphatic
items.inference: The sole nature of reality is pure, undivided knowledge.
items.plain_english: It is indeed of the one nature of pure knowledge.

items.question: Who is able to restrain that and thereby demonstrate true mastery?
premises: Restraint of that is possible
Only some are able to do it
Ability marks a special capacity
items.inference: The one capable of restraining that possesses true mastery.
items.plain_english: Whoever is able to restrain that—he then can restrain it.

rows.grounds: by the very steady and wise

items.question: By which wise ones can that be restrained through steady capacity?
premises: Restraint is possible
It requires steadiness and wisdom
Only such wise ones can accomplish it
items.inference: Only the steady and wise are capable of effecting that restraint.
items.plain_english: By which steady, wise ones it can be restrained.

items.question: By what means was Śaṅkara obtained according to this declaration?
premises: Śaṅkara is said to be obtained
The attainment occurred through a means
That means is identified as decisive
items.inference: The verse declares that Śaṅkara was attained through that specific means.
items.plain_english: By that means I obtained Śaṅkara.
